chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), the drinker of wine is to be whipped eighty (lashes) and the drinker of Al-Nabeez is to be whipped eighty (lashes).'

key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: Nabeez (fermented drink, typically from dates or grapes)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed punishment for drinking wine and nabeez according to the Book of Ali?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic view that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) prescribed a uniform penalty of eighty lashes for both wine (khamr) and nabeez, distinguishing this specific ruling from the general consensus of eighty lashes for all intoxicants. It reflects the early Shia scholarly tradition of deriving legal precedents directly from the Imam's written decrees, emphasizing the consistency in penalizing different types of fermented drinks under the same hadd. This hadith is significant for understanding the historical development of Islamic penal law regarding intoxicants within the Shia fiqh framework.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad Bin Usman, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying that in the Book of Aliasws, the drinker of the wine is to be whipped eighty (lashes) and the drinker of Al-Nabeez is to be whipped eighty (lashes)’.
